diagrams.title: Control the Vehicle-to-Cash Chain
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating steps for investor vehicles, qualified drivers, and reconciled collections.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The asset-light model assumes documented owner authority and platform acceptance of each vehicle and arrangement. Gross operator billings mean driver leases, dispatch, and co-hosting charges; passenger trip GMV and investor vehicle values remain outside this revenue measure.
diagrams.caption: A top-of-waterfall lease is a contractual collection priority, not an automatic platform capability. Use Uber fleet settlement features only where the account supports the documented split; otherwise reconcile authorized collections separately.

stages.label: Secure vehicle authority
stages.value: Document ownership and permitted commercial use before listing
stages.detail: Capture VIN, title or lease authority, lender restrictions, owner settlement terms, and responsibility for depreciation. Reject vehicles whose financing or insurance excludes the intended rental, livery, or rideshare activity.

stages.label: Qualify driver and operation
stages.value: Match driver credentials to vehicle and service jurisdiction
stages.detail: Verify applicable licenses, platform eligibility, MVR authorization, inspection dates, airport access, and policy endorsements. Treat personal use, app-on waiting, accepted trips, and passenger carriage as distinct exposure states.

stages.label: Execute handover and collection
stages.value: Record condition and activate expressly authorized payment instructions
stages.detail: Photograph condition, record odometer and fuel, explain deductibles and toll charges, and obtain the required payment authorization. Keep refundable security deposits in a liability ledger rather than recording them as sales.

stages.label: Monitor service and exceptions
stages.value: Convert telematics exceptions into scheduled human operating decisions
stages.detail: Use OBD-II GPS, diagnostic alerts, and maintenance mileage to schedule service. Route collision, overdue-payment, and vehicle-location exceptions to a named operator. Never remotely interrupt a moving or occupied vehicle.

stages.label: Close weekly settlements
stages.value: Reconcile billed charges, collected cash, and owner distributions
stages.detail: Match Uber settlement exports, authorized ACH receipts, toll statements, repair invoices, and owner splits to vehicle-level ledgers. Age failed collections separately and reconcile retained contribution before calculating profit.

diagrams.title: From Driver Inquiry to Settled Vehicle Week
diagrams.subtitle: One nested 100-inquiry cohort; every later stage is a subset of the preceding stage.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative counts describe a single prospect cohort, not verified acquisition performance or annual revenue capacity. Stage counts are 100, 60, 36, 18, and 12; total conversion is 12%. The first settled week can occur after day 30.
diagrams.caption: Track unique applicants rather than form submissions. Record a dated exclusion reason at each transition so insurance ineligibility, missing credentials, and payment failures do not disappear inside one blended conversion percentage.

stages.label: Inbound inquiries
stages.value: 100 unique applicants enter the dated source cohort
stages.detail: Deduplicate telephone numbers and applicant records in the CRM. Record service area, desired vehicle class, work schedule, and acquisition channel before screening.

stages.label: Operating fit established
stages.value: 60 applicants meet the initial jurisdiction and schedule criteria
stages.detail: Retain 60% of inquiries after checking intended service, license category, platform status, weekly availability, and published insurer eligibility requirements.

stages.label: Documents and screening complete
stages.value: 36 applicants complete the authorized evidence collection process
stages.detail: Retain 60% of the prior cohort after identity, license, MVR, and insurer review. Establish the permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b before ordering a consumer report.

stages.label: Vehicle offer accepted
stages.value: 18 applicants accept documented vehicle and collection terms
stages.detail: Retain 50% of screened applicants after disclosing weekly charges, deposits, deductible allocation, mileage terms, toll administration, and service downtime procedures.

stages.label: First settled week completed
stages.value: 12 drivers complete handover and produce reconciled cleared collections
stages.detail: Retain two-thirds of accepted offers only after coverage activation, vehicle inspection, completed handover, and cleared first-week collections. An executed contract alone does not qualify as a settled vehicle week.

diagrams.title: The $690,000 Base-Case Waterfall
diagrams.subtitle: $379,500 retained contribution becomes $144,900 owner profit after operator expenses.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All amounts are annual USD. Bars 1, 3, and 6 are absolute totals or subtotals; bars 2, 4, and 5 are signed deductions. Subtotals must reset the plotted running balance rather than being added again. The $180,000 and $54,600 expense categories are illustrative allocations of the canonical $234,600 residual operator expense requirement, not separately supplied estimates.
diagrams.caption: $690,000 - $310,500 = $379,500; $379,500 - $180,000 - $54,600 = $144,900. Owner profit equals 21.0% of gross billings and 38.18% of retained contribution. Apply the supplied 55% ASC 606 net-presentation convention; actual principal-versus-agent presentation follows the contracts and control analysis.

stages.label: Gross operator billings
stages.value: $690,000 annual lease, dispatch, and co-hosting charges
stages.detail: Opening total: $57,500 average monthly gross billings. Exclude underlying passenger fares, vehicle purchase values, refundable deposits, and investor capital from this operator billing measure.

stages.label: Owner splits and pass-through costs
stages.value: Subtract $310,500 distributed or passed through under contracts
stages.detail: Deduction: 45% of gross billings leaves the operator under the canonical retained-share model. Reconcile owner distributions and pass-through fleet costs individually; do not deduct these same costs again below retained contribution.

stages.label: Retained contribution subtotal
stages.value: $379,500 remains under the supplied 55% retained-share convention
stages.detail: Absolute subtotal: $31,625 average monthly retained contribution. This is the supplied net-presentation revenue basis, not owner profit and not a separate increment added to the running balance.

stages.label: Recurring operator operating costs
stages.value: Subtract $180,000 for the modeled recurring operating cost envelope
stages.detail: Deduction: $15,000 monthly covers the modeled operator labor, contractor support, software, administration, and operator-borne recurring costs. Include only costs outside the preceding owner and pass-through deduction.

stages.label: Depreciation and uninsured collision expense
stages.value: Subtract $54,600 in separately modeled operator-borne expense
stages.detail: Deduction: $4,550 monthly equivalent represents recognized depreciation where the operator bears it and uninsured collision expense. Investor-borne depreciation stays with the investor; cash transferred into a reserve is not itself expense.

stages.label: Annual owner profit total
stages.value: $144,900 equals 21.0% of gross operator billings
stages.detail: Closing total: $12,075 monthly equivalent and 38.18% of $379,500 retained contribution. Preserve the scorecard owner-profit definition; this figure is not a statement of after-personal-tax distributions or unrestricted cash.

diagrams.title: Compare Retention, Not Passenger Fare Volume
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative sub-niches measured as retained dollars per $100 of operator billings.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar represents $100 of gross operator billings before operator overhead. Equal billing weights across yields of $60, $50, $65, $45, and $55 produce the canonical 55% blended retained share. These are illustrative contract economics, not observed market yields or separate scorecard forecasts.
diagrams.caption: Collection rails affect settlement speed, fees, and reversals; they do not create the underlying yield. Maintain separate contract, payment-fee, and failed-collection fields. The canonical scenarios retain 55% regardless of this illustrative niche mix.

stages.label: Weekly rideshare driver leases
stages.value: $60 retained per $100 billed through authorized ACH collections
stages.detail: Illustrative $40 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $60 before operator overhead. Reconcile scheduled lease collections to cleared cash; an ACH initiation does not establish final payment.

stages.label: Licensed Black SUV shift dispatch
stages.value: $50 retained per $100 billed through reconciled commercial settlements
stages.detail: Illustrative $50 owner and vehicle-service allocation leaves $50 before overhead. Measure operator dispatch billings rather than all passenger fares; airport waiting and empty repositioning can destroy shift contribution.

stages.label: Investor vehicle co-hosting
stages.value: $65 retained per $100 of gross co-hosting billings
stages.detail: Illustrative $35 contractually payable owner and pass-through allocation leaves $65. Where the operator bills only a management fee in practice, reassess the billing denominator instead of importing investor receipts.

stages.label: Short-duration replacement vehicles
stages.value: $45 retained per $100 billed through documented short-term rentals
stages.detail: Illustrative $55 owner and pass-through allocation leaves $45 before overhead. Delivery labor, cleaning, charge reversals, and idle days require separate tracking; deposits remain liabilities until properly applied.

stages.label: Commercial sedan driver leases
stages.value: $55 retained per $100 billed through scheduled business collections
stages.detail: Illustrative $45 owner and pass-through allocation matches the canonical blend. Attach toll evidence to each permitted charge and distinguish recurring rent from reimbursements and separately disclosed administration fees.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Vehicle Release
diagrams.subtitle: A sequential decision path: every affirmative result advances; every failed check holds release.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four nodes are sequential predicates, not numerical risk scores. Numeric values indicate reading order. California and New York City are concrete jurisdiction examples; apply the actual operating jurisdiction, service category, and airport rules.
diagrams.caption: Release only after all four evidence sets are complete. Correct missing authority, coverage, screening, or contract terms before handover; a platform account does not replace carrier authority, insurer acceptance, or airport permission.

stages.label: Coverage matches every use state
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: hold release until endorsements are verified
stages.detail: Map off-app rental use and rideshare Periods 1, 2, and 3 to actual policy language and named insureds. California Public Utilities Code section 5433 governs specified TNC coverage periods; commercial livery use needs its own applicable coverage analysis.

stages.label: Authority matches service and location
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: remove the prohibited operating assignment
stages.detail: Check California charter-party authority under Public Utilities Code section 5371 where applicable, or NYC TLC driver, vehicle, and base requirements for the relevant service. Verify airport permissions separately; TCP and TLC credentials are not nationwide substitutes.

stages.label: Screening has a documented lawful basis
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: stop report ordering and driver assignment
stages.detail: Establish a permissible consumer-report purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b and protect motor-vehicle information under 18 U.S.C. 2721. Use employment-specific disclosure and pre-adverse procedures when applicable; apply 15 U.S.C. 1681m adverse-action notices as required.

stages.label: Contract and immobilizer controls are safe
stages.value: Yes: release vehicle; no: correct terms or disable remote immobilization
stages.detail: Use enacted state UCC Article 2A and applicable rental statutes to review lease disclosures, toll fees, and remedies. Validate state immobilizer restrictions and insurer terms; permit no remote engine shutdown, and require verified stationary, unoccupied status plus human review for any permitted starter inhibition.

diagrams.title: Four Seats at Base; Six at Scale
diagrams.subtitle: One accountable fleet lead coordinates three contractors before adding two distinct expansion seats.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time seat; C means contractor seat. Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 3 C, four people total. Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C, six people total. Each node represents one person; the last two nodes activate only in the Scaled configuration. Seat labels do not determine worker classification.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $180,000 gross, $99,000 retained, $25,200 profit at 14% gross margin and 25.45% retained margin. Base: $690,000 gross, $379,500 retained, $144,900 profit at 21.0% and 38.18%. Scaled: $1,200,000 gross, $660,000 retained, $336,000 profit at 28% and 50.91%. Scaled economics require the six-person pod.

stages.label: Fleet principal — base FT
stages.value: One full-time owner leads contracts, cash, and exception decisions
stages.detail: Own vehicle acceptance, insurer relationships, investor terms, weekly contribution review, and incident escalation. Approve settlement corrections against source evidence rather than allowing dispatch to rewrite owner allocations.

stages.label: Dispatch coordinator — base contractor
stages.value: One contractor coordinates assignments, handovers, and driver communication
stages.detail: Maintain the vehicle availability board, collect signed handover records, route platform issues, and confirm service interruptions. Escalate coverage and permit exceptions instead of assigning around them.

stages.label: Maintenance coordinator — base contractor
stages.value: One contractor schedules inspections, repairs, and downtime recovery
stages.detail: Review OBD-II alerts, mileage intervals, tire condition, repair estimates, and return-to-service evidence. Keep maintenance availability separate from paid utilization so idle vehicles remain visible.

stages.label: Settlement specialist — base contractor
stages.value: One contractor reconciles billing, tolls, and investor statements
stages.detail: Match platform exports, bank receipts, owner splits, repair invoices, and toll evidence. Produce aged receivables and deposit-liability schedules; the fleet principal reviews adjustments and payment releases.

stages.label: Operations manager — scaled FT
stages.value: Add one full-time manager only in the six-person configuration
stages.detail: Take daily dispatch supervision and service recovery from the principal. Use documented workload, incident response, and contribution capacity to justify the seat rather than hiring against gross passenger fare volume.

stages.label: Claims and onboarding specialist — scaled contractor
stages.value: Add one contractor for screening administration and incident documentation
stages.detail: Assemble authorized screening records, renewal evidence, collision photographs, insurer submissions, and recovery tracking. Keep report access restricted and separate claims documentation from settlement payment authority.

diagrams.title: Deploy $12,000–$65,000 Without Buying a Fleet
diagrams.subtitle: Four capital buckets; the rendered example totals $35,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are USD allocations for one $35,000 startup stack. Low-envelope allocations total $12,000; high-envelope allocations total $65,000. Endpoint allocations are coordinated budgets, not independently selectable cost ranges. This model assumes investor-supplied vehicles and excludes vehicle acquisitions.
diagrams.caption: Example: $10,000 + $5,000 + $8,000 + $12,000 = $35,000. Low envelope: $4,000 + $1,500 + $2,500 + $4,000 = $12,000. High envelope: $20,000 + $8,000 + $12,000 + $25,000 = $65,000. Startup cash, refundable deposits, and operating expense are different ledger categories.

stages.label: Insurance and authority funding
stages.value: $10,000 example allocation for coverage activation and operating credentials
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 in the low envelope and $20,000 in the high envelope for required insurance deposits, initial premiums, inspections, and applicable authority fees. Obtain actual quotes before accepting vehicle commitments.

stages.label: Telematics and collection infrastructure
stages.value: $5,000 example allocation for installed monitoring and billing setup
stages.detail: Allocate $1,500 low and $8,000 high for OBD-II devices, GPS installation, secure account setup, collection integration, and settlement templates. Treat later subscriptions as operating costs rather than repeatedly charging them to startup capital.

stages.label: Contracts and vehicle onboarding
stages.value: $8,000 example allocation for documented vehicle and driver activation
stages.detail: Allocate $2,500 low and $12,000 high for contract drafting, authorized screening, condition documentation, initial preparation, and handover logistics. Exclude vehicle purchase prices and investor capital contributions.

stages.label: Liquidity and collision buffer
stages.value: $12,000 example allocation retained as operating liquidity
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 low and $25,000 high for deductible liquidity, collection delays, and service interruptions. Keep customer deposits separate. Holding this cash does not reduce accounting profit; recognized expenses and actual disbursements follow their own timing.

diagrams.title: Build a Controlled Fleet Launch in 30 Days
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones create a launch-ready operation without forcing an early first deal.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone ending days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. The canonical time to first deal is 1–3 months. The sprint can finish with qualified prospects and complete documentation while insurer, licensing, or vehicle activation work continues.
diagrams.caption: Maintain the supplied $2,500–$15,000 monthly operating-cost range as a planning envelope, not a universal runway estimate. Release dates follow completed evidence; acquisition volume does not override vehicle readiness or insured operating scope.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Define the service jurisdiction and obtain written operating requirements
stages.detail: Choose one launch niche and geography. Obtain insurer quotes, identify applicable carrier or TLC authority, confirm platform vehicle requirements, and model the 55% retained share separately from passenger trip GMV. Deliver a priced launch worksheet and jurisdiction checklist.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Document owner terms and configure auditable collections and ledgers
stages.detail: Review vehicle-owner authority, draft driver terms, configure authorized payment collection, and create separate deposit, pass-through, and retained-contribution accounts. Deliver a sample owner statement that reconciles from gross billings to distributable amounts.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Run a limited qualification and vehicle-readiness rehearsal
stages.detail: Process a small authorized applicant cohort, inspect candidate vehicles, install approved telematics, and test maintenance alerts. Rehearse collision reporting, failed-payment handling, and stationary starter-inhibition controls without deploying an unsafe vehicle.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Complete a settlement rehearsal and schedule only ready handovers
stages.detail: Reconcile a labeled test dataset across billing, bank receipts, tolls, repairs, and owner splits. Where every requirement is complete, conduct a controlled handover; otherwise continue the documented 1–3 month first-deal plan without recording test collections as revenue.
